rv.q: All this unfolds over an entertainingly irreverent hour of jauntily operatic songs – there is a particularly good number about the various Victorian uses of arsenic – and bickering, bantering dialogue.
The writing is thrilling and shamelessly poetic, the setting a visual feast and nightmare of glaring neon and swirling video effects.

cn.t: Critics praise this clever, entertaining musical about the notorious Madeleine Smith case, arriving at a timely moment as Scotland abolishes its "not proven" verdict. The 60-minute lunchtime show proves riotously engaging.
